title: Tree Habitat
subtitle: Academic architecture study for a speculative vertical habitat
overview: Tree Habitat is a student-era architecture project that studies how a dense mixed-use tower could behave less like an isolated object and more like an urban habitat. Set beside Shenzhen's mangrove coast, the proposal uses root, trunk, branch and canopy metaphors to organize circulation, public program, office space, hotel use and planted sky levels into one spatial system.
storyHtml:
This project belongs to an academic studio context rather than a commercial commission. Its value is in the design question: how can a high-rise combine work, public culture, temporary stay and ecological imagination without becoming only a sealed office object?

The concept begins with mangrove structure. Mangrove roots stabilize unstable ground, filter edges and create shared habitat. Tree Habitat translates that logic into a split base for traffic and public programs, a dense trunk of work spaces, branching tower bodies and elevated gardens that act as collective pause points.

The proposal also tests circulation as a spatial ecology. Express elevators, local elevators, transfer floors and bridged commercial levels separate different users while allowing overlap around public and social programs. The drawings and model treat movement, section and program stacking as the main design material.

On this site, the project is presented as academic architecture: a learning-stage spatial study about ecology, structure, mixed use and representation. The digital model and image sequence are kept as evidence of the design process, not as proof of a completed built project.
